asks: jungler's coming bot, do we go
should we engage before he gets here
our jungler's pathing to us, what do I do
wait for jungler or go now
say: Start the fight as he arrives so they burn summoners running, or hold the wave still and wait if their jungler could be behind them.
more: A jungler walking in changes the lane even if he never lands a hit. They have to choose between fighting two against three or giving up the wave.
If both of them spend Flash or Heal to get out, that lane is open for the next few minutes and a second visit is far easier.
The trade-off is his camps. Make the visit count: have the wave where they can't reach their tower quickly.
check: Where is the wave, did their jungler show on the far side, and do they still have Flash?
breaks: Wrong if the wave is under their tower or their jungler was last seen on your side: let him farm instead and keep the wave near you.
basis: pro:Approach pressure forces the all-in

when: an objective spawns within a minute
asks: what do I do with arrow before dragon
should I save my ult for the fight
they're recalling before grubs, can I stop it
where do I use hawkshot
say: Fire the arrow at whoever is recalling before the spawn so they arrive late, or hold it for the fight if nobody is backing.
more: A cancelled recall before a spawn means that player turns up without items or doesn't turn up. That can be worth more than a stun in the fight.
Hawkshot does the scouting: send it over their jungle to find the jungler first, so your team knows which side is safe to stand on.
The cost is real. Without the arrow your team has one less way to start the fight, so only do it when someone else can engage.
check: Is someone actually recalling in view, and does your team have another way to start a fight?
breaks: Wrong if your team relies on your arrow to engage: keep it, and use Hawkshot alone to find their jungler.
basis: pro:Long-range ultimate stops the recall before a spawn

when: the enemy has dragon soul and your team has more kills and towers
asks: they got soul but we're ahead in gold, what now
how do we beat soul
they have soul, do we fight baron
we're fed but they have soul
say: Don't fight them five on five at a pit; catch their jungler or a carry first, or keep taking towers if nobody walks up alone.
more: Soul makes their even fights better for the rest of the game. Your gold only beats it when the fight starts with them a player short.
The jungler is the best target even when he's a tank. With him dead, Baron or Elder has nobody to contest the last hit.
Elder comes after soul, so the clock is against you. Use each completed item right away instead of waiting for a full build.
check: Which of them walks alone to ward or catch a wave, and are your team's stuns and Flashes up?
breaks: Wrong if your team has no way to lock one target down: then defend, clear waves and only fight at your own towers.
basis: pro:Gold lead against a finished soul

when: Elder dragon spawns within a minute
asks: elder's up but mid wave's crashing
who catches the wave before elder
do I leave the pit to clear mid
wave or elder
say: Send one player with fast clear or Teleport to kill the wave and come straight back, or all hold the pit if they're already hitting it.
more: A wave left alone takes a tower or an inhibitor while ten players stare at a dragon. One player gone briefly costs less than that.
While he's away the other four stand out of poke range and don't start it. The fight should begin when he's back.
The enemy sees the same thing. If their clearer leaves instead, that's your moment to step forward or start it.
check: How big is the wave, who clears it fastest, and has the enemy started the dragon?
breaks: Wrong if they can burst the dragon down quickly while you're four: then give the wave and contest together.
basis: pro:One player answers the wave before Elder

when: the enemy team has Ashe
asks: how do I protect my adc from ashe arrow
arrow keeps hitting our carry
what do I do against ashe ult
where do I stand in the fight
say: Stand on the line between Ashe and your carry and eat the arrow yourself, or stay on your engage angle if your carry has Cleanse.
more: The arrow stuns the champion it collides with. On a tank that's a wasted ultimate; on your carry it's usually the whole fight.
This matters most just before an objective, when they fire it to start. Step in front as they line up, then walk at them.
You give up your flank or your own engage timing to do it. That's fine when your team's plan is to keep one carry alive.
check: Where is Ashe standing, and does your carry have Cleanse or Flash up?
breaks: Wrong if their real threat is a diver already on your carry: turn and peel him instead of watching for the arrow.
basis: pro:Tank steps in front of the arrow

when: the enemy team has Mel
asks: how do I play against mel
mel keeps reflecting my ult
when do I use my ult vs mel
should I engage on mel
say: Throw a cheap ability at Mel first and wait for her reflect, then use your big projectile, or aim it at someone far from her.
more: Rebuttal sends enemy projectiles back at the attacker. A reflected stun or rocket can start the fight for her team instead of yours.
So the first thing thrown at her should be something you don't mind getting back. Once the barrier has been used, she's a normal target.
The cost is tempo: holding your ultimate a beat makes the engage slower, and she may hold the barrier just as patiently.
check: Did you see her barrier go up, and is your ability a projectile at all?
breaks: Wrong if your key ability isn't a projectile: she can't send it back, so use it on her whenever she's in range and the barrier is down.
basis: pro:Bait the reflect before the real ability

when: you got a kill or assist in a side lane in the last 3 minutes
asks: should I gank bot again
do I go back to the same lane
same lane twice?
they're still pushing bot, go again?
say: Go back while their summoners are down and they still push, or switch to your camps and the other side if they've started playing safe.
more: A lane that lost Flash and keeps shoving has learned nothing. The second and third visits are cheaper than the first because nobody can escape.
Path so your camps end next to that lane. Then each return costs you almost no farm, and their jungler must give up his own side to answer.
The limit is their jungler. After two kills he'll hover there, so the next visit may be three against three; have a ward on his approach.
check: Are they past the middle of the lane, did a ward go down in the river brush, and where was their jungler last seen?
breaks: Wrong once they hug their tower or swap that lane away: take the dragon beside it or move to the other half.
basis: pro:Keep punishing a lane that will not respect you

asks: should I just throw binding
how do I trade as morgana
I keep missing Q
when do I use dark binding
say: Hold Dark Binding so they can't walk up freely, or throw it when your jungler is near or they stop to last hit.
more: While the binding is up, an engage support has to respect you. The moment it misses, they know they have a free window on your carry.
Spamming it also empties your mana, and then neither the binding nor Black Shield is there when their jungler arrives.
Keep Black Shield for the disabling ability, not for poke. It absorbs magic damage and disabling effects, so time it on the hook or stun.
check: How much mana do you have, and has their support used his engage ability?
breaks: Wrong if they're pushed under your tower with no escape: then throw it, since a hit there is usually a kill with your carry.
basis: pro:The threat of the binding beats the binding

when: your lane has died to their jungler twice or more
asks: they keep ganking bot what do I do
we can't lane here anymore
should we swap lanes
jungler's camping us
say: Move your duo to mid, where the lane is short, or stay and farm at your tower if your mid can't hold a side lane.
more: A long lane with no summoners is where a jungler earns his whole game. Mid has a tower close behind you wherever the wave is.
Your mid laner takes the side lane instead. That works when he has an escape or wave clear; it's rough on an immobile mage.
It also sets up the next dragon: a marksman clearing mid quickly gives your team first move to the river.
check: Is the wave about to crash so you can leave without losing it, and can your mid survive alone in the side lane?
breaks: Wrong if their duo would simply stay and take every plate behind you: then hold the tower and ask for a ward instead.
basis: pro:Swap the duo out of a camped lane

when: your team killed a dragon in the last 30 seconds, it is after 8:00 and grubs have not been taken
asks: we got dragon, now what
do I go grubs after drake
dragon done, back or grubs
can we get both
say: If mid is still shoved, run straight to grubs before they reset, or recall and spend if you're low or their top side is waiting.
more: A team that sent three or four players to stop the dragon has nobody near the top pit. That gap closes as soon as they recall.
Mid push is what makes it work. Your mid walks up with you; theirs has to choose between the wave and a fight he arrives late to.
Grubs don't respawn, so two objectives in one rotation is a lead that shows up later as faster towers.
check: Is your mid wave pushed, how healthy are you, and did their top and jungler show bot?
breaks: Wrong if you'd arrive low with Smite down: recall, and let your top take plates while they walk back.
basis: pro:One objective straight into the next

when: the enemy team has two or more dive champions
asks: what do I build against their dive
they just jump on me every time
health or damage first
should I build tanky as a mage
say: Take a health item first so one combo doesn't kill you and you can keep shoving, or go damage if they can't reach you.
more: With extra health you can stand in a side lane and trade into an assassin, because he can no longer finish you in one go.
That keeps three lanes pushing, which is how your team gets to objectives first. Dead mages don't have priority.
The price comes later: your burst arrives an item late, so fights around the second or third dragon lean more on your marksman.
check: Who on their team can actually reach you, and how much of their damage is burst?
breaks: Wrong if you're the only real damage on your team: buy damage and stay behind your front line instead.
basis: pro:Health first to keep the push

when: you have at least two more kills than deaths and an objective spawns within two minutes
asks: I'm fed, how do I use it
how do I carry as an assassin
what do I do with my lead
they all have flash, who do I kill
say: Go dark near the next objective and chunk one carry before it spawns, or shove a side lane first if they've all still got Flash.
more: Burst champions are strongest while they're an item ahead. That window closes, so each minute without a kill is a minute your damage falls behind.
When everyone has Flash it takes two steps: the first combo forces the Flash, and the second, a little later, gets the kill.
Fog is the weapon. Once they don't know where you are, their carries stop walking to wards and waves alone, and your team gets the pit.
check: Which carries have used Flash, and is the brush you want to sit in already warded?
breaks: Wrong if they have point-and-click lockdown saved for you: stay with your team and go in second, after it's used.
basis: pro:Burst leads expire, spend them before the objective

when: you have Teleport and a dragon is up
asks: should I tp to dragon
do I teleport bot for the fight
tp now or keep it
is it worth tping to drake
say: Teleport if it makes the numbers and secures the dragon, or keep it and take plates if your team already has more players there.
more: A committed Teleport usually scares the other team off the pit. The direct cost is small: a few minions while you walk back.
The hidden cost is the next few minutes. If their mid still has Teleport, the next objective or dive is his to join first.
After using it, play the following spawn safer: shove early and walk, because you can't arrive late any more.
check: How many from each team are at the pit, and does their mid still have Teleport?
breaks: Wrong if the fight is already lost or the dragon is nearly dead: stay and take the tower plates instead.
basis: pro:Teleport to the pit, then respect the cooldown gap

asks: their support left lane, what do we do
support's roaming, can we fight
it's a 2v1 bot now
their supp is missing
say: Hit their marksman hard right now while it's two on one, or shove and take a plate if he's hiding at tower.
more: A roaming support buys his mid a play and pays with his own lane. The punishment has to land before he walks back.
Trade when the support is seen elsewhere and disengage as he returns; the returning support often arrives from the river behind you.
Even without a kill, a forced Heal or lost health means the next wave is yours, and that's push for the first dragon.
check: Was their support actually seen in another lane, and where is their jungler?
breaks: Wrong if nobody has seen the support: he may be in the lane brush, so ward it before stepping up.
basis: pro:Punish the lane the support left

when: a soul-point dragon or Elder spawns within two minutes and you have gold left after your last item
asks: what do I buy before soul fight
I've got extra gold, what now
should I buy an elixir
spare gold before elder
say: Spend the leftover on an elixir and control wards for this one fight, or save it only if your next item is a recall away.
more: Gold in your pocket does nothing in the fight that decides soul. A temporary boost that wins it is worth more than a faster item afterwards.
Control wards matter as much: the team that sees the flank picks the first target.
If the fight goes badly you've lost a little gold. If it goes well, the soul or Elder is worth far more than what you spent.
check: How close is your next completed item, and how long until the spawn?
breaks: Wrong if you can finish a full item with one more wave before the spawn: farm that wave and buy the item.
basis: pro:Spend everything on the fight that decides soul

when: you have Exhaust and an enemy assassin or burst mage leads their team in kills
asks: who do I exhaust
when do I use exhaust
exhaust the tank or the assassin
their mid one-shots us
say: Hold Exhaust for their fed assassin the moment he jumps in, or use it on their marksman if the assassin is dead or far away.
more: Burst champions do their damage in one short window. Exhaust inside that window turns a kill into a survived combo, and then he's stuck in your team.
It means staying near your carry and not spending the spell on the first tank who walks up.
The trade-off is your own engage: a support guarding the carry starts fewer fights, so someone else has to.
check: Where is their assassin, and who is he most likely to jump on?
breaks: Wrong if he's far behind in items: then use Exhaust on whoever is doing the most damage.
basis: pro:Exhaust is for the burst, not the front line

when: your lane opponent is a champion with strong self-healing
asks: should I buy anti heal
do I rush grievous wounds
he just heals everything back
anti heal now or later
say: Buy the cheap healing-reduction part now if you hit him every trade, or finish your first item first if he can just back off and wait.
more: Healing reduction only works while it's applied. A champion who heals between fights can step away, let it wear off and then heal.
So it pays in long fights and all-ins, and pays little in a poke lane. Early on, a delayed first item is a real cost.
In team fights it's best on whoever hits the healer most. If your team has one magic damage dealer, he's often the right buyer.
check: Does he heal during the fight or after it, and how far are you from your first item?
breaks: Wrong if he's their main threat and fights you constantly: then finish the full healing-reduction item early.
basis: pro:Anti-heal only counts while it is applied

when: before 4:00
asks: he's in my jungle, what do I do
their jungler's taking my camps
I got invaded level 1
do I fight him at my buff
say: Cross and take the half he left so you stay even on camps, or fight him only if your nearest laner is already walking over.
more: He can't be in two places. Every camp he takes from you leaves one of his own standing on the other side.
Swapping halves also decides which lane you live next to for the next few minutes. Tell that lane, and tell the other one it's alone.
Fighting him needs help. Early duels are decided by which mid or support arrives first, not by the two junglers.
check: Which of your camps are gone, is your mid pushed in, and which of his camps should still be up?
breaks: Wrong if his laners on that side have push and can collapse on you: take whatever of yours is left and recall for an item.
basis: pro:Answer an invade by swapping halves

when: you are level 6, their jungler is level 5 and grubs spawn within a minute
asks: I hit six first, what do I do
should I invade before grubs
I'm 6 he's 5
fight him or start grubs
say: Find him at his own buff now, while your ultimate is up and his isn't, or go straight to grubs if you don't know his side.
more: One level here is a whole ultimate. Even if he lives, he usually leaves Flash and the buff behind.
Then the grub fight starts with their jungler low, without Flash and still without his ultimate. That's the real payoff.
It costs you a few seconds of setup at the pit. Do it only if your lanes can reach you before his can.
check: Which side did he last show on, is his buff due, and which of your lanes have push?
breaks: Wrong if he's about to finish the level on his next camp: go to the pit and set up instead.
basis: pro:Use the level six gap just before the spawn

when: an ally died in the last 10 seconds and your team has more players dead than theirs
asks: he got caught, do I go help
should I tp to that fight
they're fighting without me
do I follow up
say: Don't join one at a time; take a tower or camps on the other side while they're busy, or go only if you all arrive together.
more: A failed gank turns into a lost fight when each ally walks in after the last one died. The enemy gets a kill for every arrival.
While four of them chase, something of theirs is unguarded. A tower or their jungle camps is a real answer, and it's safe.
The exception is a full group move: if three of you can reach it at once with ultimates, the numbers flip.
check: How many enemies showed at the fight, and what is open on the far side?
breaks: Wrong if the caught ally is still alive under your tower: then go, because the tower makes up the numbers.
basis: pro:Do not feed a lost skirmish one body at a time

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: I got his flash, now what
he has no flash, do I all in
how do I use his flash being down
ping jungler or go myself
say: Tell your jungler, then go in again the moment your ultimate is back, or just shove and roam if he's hugging tower now.
more: If your ultimate bought his Flash, the two timers aren't equal: yours usually returns before his does. The second attempt has no escape in it.
If he flashed without you spending anything, the window is open right now. That's the better case, so call the gank at once.
He'll play far back, which gives you the wave. Free push is also a roam or first move to the river.
check: Did you spend your ultimate to get the Flash, and where is their jungler?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is sitting mid to cover him: push the wave and take your lead to a side lane.
basis: pro:Time the second go for when the ultimate returns

when: an ally died under their own tower in the last 30 seconds
asks: they dove bot, do we dive top
should we answer with our own dive
can we trade a dive
they're all bot, dive mid?
say: Answer with your own dive only if the target dies fast; otherwise take plates or grubs, which don't need a kill.
more: Their dive is already finishing when yours starts. If yours takes long, their winners walk over and arrive while you're still under the tower.
A fast answer needs a target without Flash and a wave already crashing. Missing either one, it becomes a second lost play.
Plates, a tower or grubs pay the same way without that risk, and you can leave them the moment the divers come looking.
check: Does your target have Flash or a defensive ultimate, and is your wave at his tower?
breaks: Wrong if their divers are low and far away: then the dive is safe, so take the kill and the tower.
basis: pro:An answering dive has to be quick

when: your team is ahead in kills and is taking an objective
asks: what's my job at the objective
do I hit baron or zone
where do I stand while they take it
they're coming to contest, what do I do
say: Stand between them and the pit and let them come at you while your team finishes, or back into the pit if you'd die first.
more: A healing bruiser who soaks the engage does two jobs: the objective keeps dropping, and their cooldowns land on the wrong target.
You don't have to start anything. Let them use everything on you, then your team turns from the pit with full health and ultimates.
It works when you're ahead and have sustain. On even items, five people will just kill you, so stay closer.
check: Are your Flash and ultimate up, and how close is your team to finishing?
breaks: Wrong if their carries can hit you from range without walking in: stay in the pit and help burst it.
basis: pro:Soak the engage while the team finishes

when: your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: how do we come back
we're losing every fight, what now
how do I get a pick when behind
where do I set up
say: Wait in a brush on their path back from base and catch whoever walks first, or hold your towers if you can't see their jungler.
more: Leading teams get careless on the way back from base: carries walk through the jungle alone because it feels safe.
One carry dead, especially one with no Flash, turns the next objective into a fight you can take.
The risk is being found. Go with two or three, use a control ward so you aren't seen, and leave if nobody comes.
check: Did you see them recall, which entrance do they use, and is that brush warded?
breaks: Wrong if they move as five: then nobody walks first, so farm waves and defend until they split.
basis: pro:Catch the carry on the walk back from base

when: your team is behind in kills
asks: we have no tank, who goes first
how do we get vision when behind
we can't face check anything
who checks the bush
say: Check brushes with abilities and fight only where they must walk to you, or give the pit and defend if nothing can scout.
more: Without a front line, the first player into fog is the first one dead, and then it's four against five at the spawn.
Clones, flags, traps and long-range shots can tell you if a brush is full. That's information, but someone still has to engage after.
So choose fights at your own tower or a narrow entrance they have to cross. Let their engage come to your abilities.
check: Which abilities on your team reveal or zone a brush, and which paths to the pit are dark?
breaks: Wrong at their soul-point dragon: that one you must contest, so go early as five and ward before they arrive.
basis: pro:No front line means no face checks

asks: I'm on the flank, when do I go
they saw me flanking, now what
should I engage now or wait
do I go in from behind
say: Go when your team is close enough to follow, or walk out and rejoin them if a ward spots you before that.
more: A flank is worth a lot because it's unseen. Once they know, they turn on you first and your team arrives to a lost fight.
The mistake is going anyway because you're already there. An early engage drags your team into a fight at the wrong time.
Walking out costs nothing but the angle. You can try another side once your team has cleared a ward.
check: Did you cross a ward, and how far is your team from the fight?
breaks: Wrong if their carry is alone and in range right now: then go, since the kill is quicker than their reaction.
basis: pro:A spotted flank is a cancelled flank

when: their carry has Zhonya's Hourglass or Guardian Angel
asks: he has zhonyas, how do I kill him
they bought GA, what now
how do I dive the carry late
he just goes gold and I die
say: Make him use the stasis first with a short threat, then go again, or switch to the carry who hasn't bought one.
more: Late defensive items give a carry a second life. A dive that spends everything on the first one has nothing left for the second.
So split it: one ability or one teammate forces the item, and the real damage arrives after it ends.
A dive team gets weaker as these items appear. If you're ahead, end before they're finished; if not, pick the target without one.
check: Which enemy carries have those items in their list, and did you see them used recently?
breaks: Wrong if you can't survive long enough for a second go: stay on the front line and hit what reaches you.
basis: pro:Defensive items punish an all-in dive

when: an enemy has Zhonya's Hourglass or Guardian Angel
asks: how do I deal with zhonyas as cait
what do I do when he goes gold
where do my traps go in fights
he revived, now what
say: Put a trap under anyone in stasis or reviving so they wake up caught, or keep traps at your feet if a diver is on you.
more: Yordle Snap Trap immobilizes whoever springs it and gives you an empowered Headshot. Someone coming out of stasis is standing right on it.
That turns their best defensive item into a delay. Your team should hold damage until the trap fires.
The trade-off is your own safety: a trap spent forward isn't guarding you, so do it when their divers are already used up.
check: Is anyone threatening you right now, and do you have a trap ready?
breaks: Wrong if you'd have to walk into their team to place it: stay back and keep hitting the nearest target.
basis: pro:Trap under the stasis

when: your team has Baron buff and the enemy has three dragons
asks: we got baron but they're on soul point
do we siege or go dragon
baron or stop their soul
where do we use baron
say: Use Baron on the two lanes nearest the dragon, then be at the pit before it spawns, or keep sieging if it's over two minutes away.
more: Without their soul point you could ignore the dragon and push the far lanes. With it, the dragon decides how long your lead lasts.
Pushing the near lanes does both jobs: towers fall, and those waves keep their players at home when the dragon appears.
If the buff would run out during the fight anyway, don't waste it standing at the pit early; take what you can first.
check: How long until the dragon, and which lanes still have their outer towers?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is dead with a long timer: take the dragon the moment it's up, then go back to the siege.
basis: pro:Baron against a soul point

when: the enemy has Baron buff
asks: they have baron, what do we do
how do we defend baron push
should we fight them at our tower
do we give the inhib
say: Kill every wave from behind your towers and don't walk out, or give an inhibitor before you take a fight into the buff.
more: The buff is a timer. Each wave you clear safely is one fewer push, and the buff ends whether or not they got anything.
Stepping past your last outer tower is how it goes wrong: out there they can come at you from two sides.
An inhibitor comes back; five deaths with Baron on them can be the game. Fight when the buff ends or at the next dragon.
check: How long is left on their buff, and who on your team clears waves safely?
breaks: Wrong if one of them is caught alone at the start: then fight at once, five on four under your tower.
basis: pro:Outlast the Baron buff

asks: he flashed away low, do I chase
should I finish the kill
one hp, chase or turn
keep chasing him?
say: Let him go and turn to whoever is still in the fight, or chase only if your carry is safe and one hit finishes it.
more: A low target running away has already left the fight. Three players following him have left it too, and theirs haven't.
Meanwhile their divers get free time on your back line. Fights flip this way after a perfect opening.
The kill is worth gold; the fight is worth the objective. Take the second, and the first often comes back anyway.
check: Who on their team is still fighting, and is your carry being hit?
breaks: Wrong if he's their only damage and everyone else is dead: then run him down.
basis: pro:Do not chase the one who got away

when: your team is ahead in kills and an objective spawns within two minutes
asks: should I take their camps
what do I do between objectives when ahead
can I invade now
how do I starve their jungler
say: Take their camps on your way to warding the next pit, or stay on your own side if two of their lanes are pushing.
more: When you're ahead, their jungle is spare gold for you and the only safe gold for their jungler. Taking it widens the level gap.
Do it on the objective side, so the same trip leaves wards on their route to the pit.
The danger is greed: at a deep camp with their waves pushing, their laners arrive before yours can.
check: Which of their camps are up, where are the side waves, and how many enemies are showing?
breaks: Wrong if you'd be alone and several enemies are missing: ward the entrance and leave.
basis: pro:Starve the jungler on the way to the pit

asks: my mid has no flash, should I help
should I roam mid
mid's getting ganked a lot
do I leave my adc to ward mid
say: Walk mid, ward both sides and help shove one wave, then go back, or stay bot if your carry can't be left alone.
more: A mid laner without Flash is the easiest gank on the map. Two wards and a pushed wave make him hard to reach for a while.
That push also lets your jungler start the dragon with mid able to move first. It's a short trip with a long payoff.
Your carry loses your protection for a wave or two, so go when your own wave is pushed out or right after a recall.
check: Has your mid used Flash, where is your bot wave, and is their jungler likely on your side?
breaks: Wrong if their bot lane can all-in your carry while you're gone: stay, and ping your jungler toward mid instead.
basis: pro:Cover the mid laner who has no Flash

when: your support is an enchanter
asks: who starts the fight on our team
nobody engages, what do I do
should I go in first
we have no engage
say: You're the engage: walk at them first and trust the shields behind you, or wait at your carry if your team is too far to follow.
more: An enchanter keeps people alive but can't start anything. If the tank doesn't go, the fight starts on their terms.
Your job is to be hit first and survive long enough for your team to walk in behind. Shields and heals make that much easier.
The risk is distance: a tank who charges far ahead of his team is just a delay before a four against five.
check: How far behind you is your team, and are your engage abilities up?
breaks: Wrong if you're in a side lane with no Teleport ready: then your jungler has to start it.
basis: pro:With an enchanter, the tank is the engage

when: your team has Baron buff
asks: how do we siege with baron safely
where do I ward during the push
they keep flanking our siege
what do I do as support with baron
say: Ward the jungle entrances beside the tower before anyone hits it, or pull back a step if one side is still dark.
more: A losing team's best fight is a flank or a Teleport behind your siege. One missing ward is enough for it to work.
Clear and ward both sides first, then hit the tower. It costs a little of the buff and removes their only good play.
Sweep for a ward behind you as well: a Teleport needs something to land on.
check: Which entrances near this tower have no ward, and who on their team has Teleport?
breaks: Wrong if the buff has only seconds left: take the tower shots you can and reset.
basis: pro:Close the flank before the siege

when: you have Teleport and your team is behind in towers
asks: how do I get to their carry
where do I tp in a siege
should I flank with tp
we need a miracle fight
say: Teleport to a ward behind them as they siege and hit the carry from the back, or defend from the front if no ward is left.
more: A team pushing your tower faces forward. A diver arriving behind splits their attention, and your team at the tower can step out.
It needs a ward they missed and a team ready to go the moment you land. Call it before you channel.
If it fails you're dead far from help and the tower likely falls. That's acceptable when the alternative is losing slowly anyway.
check: Is there a ward of yours behind them, and can your team engage when you arrive?
breaks: Wrong if they turn toward the Teleport before it finishes: drop the idea next time and clear waves from the front.
basis: pro:The Teleport flank on a siege

asks: how do we get a pick
how do I bait them
nobody's walking up, what do I do
how to set a trap
say: Have one ally show on a ward farming or recalling while you wait unseen beside him, or just hold vision if they don't bite.
more: A visible target who looks alone invites the dive. Whoever comes for him walks into your engage with your team a few steps away.
A control ward makes it work: clear their ward on your brush, so they see the bait and not you.
If they don't come, you've lost a few seconds. If they do, the kill usually comes with a shutdown and the next objective.
check: Do they have vision of the bait but not of you, and is your team close enough to follow?
breaks: Wrong if the bait is your only carry and they have long-range burst: use a tank or a mobile champion as bait.
basis: pro:Bait on a ward, engage from the dark

asks: we went in and they all flashed
first engage failed, do we go again
they used everything, now what
keep fighting or back off
say: Step back a moment, then go again while their Flashes are down, or leave if your own front line is too low.
more: The first engage doesn't have to kill. If it takes their summoners and they're still standing there, the second one has no answer.
This is why engaging in two layers works: one player goes, comes out, and the next goes onto the same target.
It only holds while the cooldowns are down and your team is healthy. Wait too long and it's a new fight.
check: Who used Flash or a stasis item, and how healthy is your front line?
breaks: Wrong if your first engager died: then it's four against five, so take what's safe and go.
basis: pro:Engage in two layers

when: your team is ahead in kills
asks: their jungler walked in alone, do we kill him
is this a bait
should we collapse on him
he's by himself, go?
say: Take him only if he dies before their ultimates land on your group, or step off and keep the pit if their mages are behind him.
more: A tanky player walking into five is often the opening for area ultimates. Everyone who piles onto him stands in one spot.
One fight like that can erase a lead built over many minutes, and it gives their scaling carries the gold they were missing.
When you're ahead you don't need the kill. Holding the objective makes them walk in properly, on your terms.
check: Where are their area-damage ultimates, and are your teammates standing spread out?
breaks: Wrong if their damage dealers are showing in other lanes: then he's simply caught, so kill him.
basis: pro:The lone tank is the bait

asks: when do I engage
I went in and nobody followed
should I wait for my adc
why do my engages fail
say: Engage only when your carry is in range behind you, or hold your ground and peel if he's still walking up.
more: A front-to-back team wins by its carry hitting from behind the tanks. An engage he can't reach is a fight without your damage.
Patience is the whole plan when you're ahead: stand in front of him, let them come, and the lead does the work.
The trade-off is giving them the first move. That's acceptable if you have a way to stop their diver once he commits.
check: Where is your main carry, and can he reach the target you want?
breaks: Wrong if their carry is caught with no Flash right next to you: go, and ping your team onto him.
basis: pro:Do not engage ahead of your carry

when: you got a kill or assist in the last 20 seconds and your health is below 40 percent
asks: we got the kill, can I do grubs
I'm low, do I start dragon
kill done, objective or back
can I take it at this health
say: Recall first, or shove the wave with your laner; start the objective only if their jungler is dead or showed far away.
more: A jungler who tanked tower shots for a kill is a free second kill at the pit. Then the objective goes to them and the play was for nothing.
The kill still pays: plates, a crashed wave, or a clean recall into an item all come without risk.
If their jungler is dead, it changes. Even low, you can take it, because nobody can contest the last hit.
check: Where is their jungler, is Smite up, and can a laner tank the objective for you?
breaks: Wrong if a healthy laner can tank it and two more allies are already there: then start it and stand at the back.
basis: pro:Low after the dive, skip the objective

asks: he still has flash, is the gank worth it
should I gank if I can't kill him
gank mid or keep farming
is a no-kill gank ok
say: Go if your laner's wave is about to hit his tower, since pushing him off costs him that wave, or farm if it's mid-lane.
more: A gank doesn't need a kill to pay. If he has to walk away while a wave dies at his tower, he loses gold and experience.
It's cheapest when the lane is next to the camp you just finished, so the visit takes seconds from your clear.
It also shows him where you are. Tell the far-side lane to play back for the next half minute.
check: Where is the wave, and how far is the lane from your next camp?
breaks: Wrong if it pulls you away from camps that are up while their jungler farms: clear first, then look.
basis: pro:A gank that only denies the wave still pays

when: you got a kill in the last minute
asks: I flashed for the kill, now what
I have no flash mid
how do I play with flash down
am I gankable now
say: Stand on the side of the lane away from their jungler and ward the other, or shove and recall if you can't see him.
more: Spending Flash for a kill is usually right, but the bill arrives a minute later, when their jungler and support look at mid.
Your gold lead doesn't help if you can't get out. Position first, damage second, until Flash is back.
Ask your jungler to stay near for one clear. A counter-gank on the player they expect to be free is often two kills.
check: Did you actually use Flash, and where did their jungler last show?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler just showed on the far side: keep pushing and trade freely for that short window.
basis: pro:The bill for an offensive Flash

when: the enemy team has two or more champions with area-engage ultimates
asks: how do we fight their wombo
they just ult all of us
where do I stand against aoe
how do we beat their teamfight
say: Stand apart, let the first one jump in and kill him, then fight, or start it yourselves if their ultimates were just used.
more: Area ultimates need you clumped and need to land together. Spread out, the first engager hits one or two and is alone.
Kill him quickly and the rest of their combination has no setup. The clean-up after that is where sustained damage wins.
Narrow river entrances and pits are where they want you. Fight in the open or make them come through the choke.
check: Which of their big ultimates are up, and how close together is your team standing?
breaks: Wrong if you have the stronger engage and they're the ones clumped: then go first.
basis: pro:Absorb the first engage, then clean up

asks: they're teleporting in, what do we do
tp behind us, fight or run
do we finish the objective or turn
someone's tping to the fight
say: Stop hitting the objective and stand on the Teleport so he lands into all of you, or finish it if it's nearly dead.
more: A player arriving by Teleport lands alone for a moment, usually before his team has walked up. Five on one is a free start.
Killing him also removes the reason their team was going to fight. They back off, and the objective is yours a few seconds later.
If you ignore it and keep hitting, he lands behind you while the objective is lowering your team's health.
check: Where is the Teleport landing, how low is the objective, and how close is the rest of their team?
breaks: Wrong if their whole team is already in your face: then fight the front and keep one player watching the back.
basis: pro:Turn on the Teleport

when: you are level 3 or higher
asks: when do I roam mid
should I go with my jungler
roam or stay bot
can I leave lane now
say: Roam when your wave is shoved and your jungler is heading mid too, or stay if your carry would be alone against two.
more: Support and jungler arriving together is the strongest early play on the map. Mid can't fight three, and Flash usually goes.
A support roaming alone mostly just loses experience. Time it with your jungler's path, not with your own boredom.
Your carry pays for it, so leave on a pushed wave and come back before the next one arrives.
check: Where is your jungler going next, and is your bot wave pushed out?
breaks: Wrong if your carry is behind and their lane has kill pressure: stay and ward for your jungler instead.
basis: pro:Roam with the jungler, not alone

asks: where do I go when mid split pushes
who do I stay with mid game
where do I ward for our split pusher
do I stay with adc
say: Stand between mid and your split pusher's lane and ward a line on that side, or stay with your carry if he's being dived.
more: Wards in a row across one half of the map let the side laner see a collapse coming with time to leave.
From that spot you can reach him or mid quickly, so your presence covers both. He can play much further forward.
The other half of the map goes dark. Your team should treat that side as theirs and not walk into it.
check: Which side is your split pusher on, and can your carry clear mid safely without you?
breaks: Wrong if the next objective is on the other side: move your wards there a minute before it spawns.
basis: pro:Lean toward the split pusher's side

when: you have Teleport and an objective spawns within a minute
asks: can I keep split pushing
should I group for dragon
do I tp or walk
split or group
say: Keep pushing the far lane if Teleport is ready and a ward is near the pit, or start walking now if either is missing.
more: A side wave pushed deep makes one of them stay home, and you can still be at the fight in seconds.
The enemy watches the same thing. If they see you far away without Teleport, they start the objective that moment.
Tell your team to wait for your channel. A fight that begins before you press it is four against five.
check: Is your Teleport actually off cooldown, and is there a ward or minion to land on?
breaks: Wrong if your team is already being forced into the fight: teleport now, even if the wave isn't finished.
basis: pro:Split only as far as Teleport reaches

when: you do not have Teleport and an objective spawns within a minute
asks: no tp, can I still split
do I leave lane for baron
they're starting it and I'm bot
push tower or go to team
say: Leave the lane now and walk, or stay only if you're taking a tower and your team has agreed to give the objective.
more: Seen far away with no Teleport, you've told them it's five on four. Good teams start the objective immediately.
If you stay, make it a real trade: a tower or inhibitor, not a wave. And your team must not fight.
Walking early costs a wave. Arriving late costs the objective and usually a teammate.
check: How long is the walk, and what can you actually finish before they do?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is dead: your team can take it without you, so keep pushing.
basis: pro:No Teleport, no deep split

when: after 8:00, grubs have not been taken and the enemy team has a split-push champion
asks: grubs or dragon first
can I give grubs for drake
which objective matters more here
do I trade grubs
say: Don't hand grubs to a split-push team; contest or take a share, or trade them for dragon only if they have no strong side laner.
more: Grubs help break towers. A team built to push side lanes turns that into fallen towers much faster than a team-fight group does.
They're one window from 8:00 and don't come back, so what you give here stays given.
Taking even a share is fine. The point is their duelist shouldn't get the full set and a free lane.
check: Who are their side laners, and can your top and mid get to the pit first?
breaks: Wrong if contesting means a fight you lose: take the dragon and plan to send two players at their split pusher later.
basis: pro:Grubs are worth more to a split-push team

when: you are level 10 or level 15 and an objective spawns within a minute
asks: should we wait before fighting
I'm almost 11, does it matter
one more camp before dragon?
fight now or level first
say: Take one more camp or wave for the level before you fight, or go now if your team is already outnumbered there.
more: The next level ranks up your ultimate on most champions. Fighting just before it is giving away a spike for no reason.
It works for them too: if their key player is one level short, start before he gets it.
The cost is seconds. If the camp is on the way to the pit, it's free; if it's across the map, skip it.
check: How close is your experience bar to the next level, and is a camp or wave on your route?
breaks: Wrong if the objective is already being hit: go at once, because the level won't matter after it's gone.
basis: pro:Hit the ultimate rank before the fight

asks: what do I spell shield
how do I lane as sivir
when do I use E
they keep engaging on me
say: Save Spell Shield for their engage ability and push with everything else, or use it on poke if neither of them can start a fight.
more: Spell Shield blocks one enemy ability and gives you health and a burst of speed when it does. On an engage, that cancels their whole play.
With that held, you can shove every wave. Sivir's push is what gets her team to the river first.
It all depends on gold: when she's behind, her wave clear is slow and the shield is the main thing keeping her in lane.
check: Which of their abilities starts the fight, and have they used it?
breaks: Wrong against an engage that isn't a single ability aimed at you: then stand further back and let your support absorb it.
basis: pro:The shield is for the engage

asks: which lane do I play for
who do I get ahead
top or bot focus
which laner should I camp
say: Play for the laner who can dive a carry with you later, or for bot if your team needs dragons and their duo is weak.
more: Two divers hitting the same target at once is how a carry dies through his summoners. Getting your partner ahead makes that reliable.
The cost is the other side. A fed top laner doesn't give your marksman wave control, and without it dragons are hard.
And their tank top can ignore a lost lane and just push towers. Your lead has to be used in fights, soon.
check: Which of your laners has lockdown or a dash to follow you, and which enemy lane has no Flash?
breaks: Wrong if that laner's opponent is a tank who doesn't mind dying: the kills buy little, so go where a carry is.
basis: pro:Feed the partner you will dive with

when: you have at least two more kills than your lane opponent
asks: I'm fed top but he just pushes
how do I use my lead top
should I group or split when ahead
he ignores me and takes towers
say: Take his tower, then bring the lead to the next objective with your ultimate up, or match him if he's taking yours for free.
more: A tank who lost lane still does his job in fights. Your kills only matter if they kill a carry before his team's items catch up.
If you leave and he keeps pushing, he trades towers for your presence. Check that the fight you join is worth a tower.
Arriving without your ultimate wastes the trip. Wait in lane for it, then move.
check: Is your ultimate up, where is the side wave, and what does he take if you leave?
breaks: Wrong if no objective is up for a couple of minutes: stay, deny him the wave and take plates.
basis: pro:A top lead has to reach a carry

when: an enemy top laner or jungler has three or more kills
asks: their top is fed, where do I farm
which lane do I go mid game
I keep getting dove in side lane
mid or side as adc
say: Farm the lane he isn't in, with your support beside you, or stay mid under tower if you can't tell where he is.
more: A fed diver kills a marksman alone in one combination. The answer is not to be the one standing opposite him.
Let your tank or a safe mage take his lane. You keep your gold coming, and he gets nothing worth diving.
It may mean a slower lane for you. That's cheaper than a death that also hands him your shutdown.
check: Which lane did he last show in, and who on your team can hold him?
breaks: Wrong if he's grouped with his team: then stay behind your front line and farm whichever wave is nearest.
basis: pro:Keep the carry out of the fed diver's lane

when: their support is a tanky engage champion
asks: their support's out of position, kill him?
should we focus the tank
leona's in front, hit her?
who do I hit
say: Hit him only while he's the one in reach and keep your abilities, or turn fully if he's really alone with no team behind.
more: An engage support standing in front wants your cooldowns. He survives a long time, and while you unload on him their damage walks in.
Basic attacks on him are fine. The stuns, dashes and ultimates stay ready for the carry who follows.
If his team truly isn't there, he's a kill and often the objective after. It's the commit that needs the check, not the first hit.
check: Where are their damage dealers, and how long would he take to die?
breaks: Wrong if he's low and they have no way to reach you: finish him and take the numbers advantage.
basis: pro:Do not unload on the tank in front

when: you are at least two levels above their marksman
asks: we crushed level 1, now what
he's stuck level 1, how do I press it
do we dive or freeze
how do I snowball this lane
say: Stand between him and the wave so he gets no experience, or shove and recall for an item if their jungler is coming.
more: Early on, a level gap is worth more than the gold. A marksman two levels down can't fight, can't push and can't help his jungler.
Hold the wave just outside his tower and he has to choose between losing it and losing health.
It only works while their jungler is elsewhere. Zoning that far up with no ward is how a won lane hands the kills back.
check: Where did their jungler start, is there a ward in the river, and do they have Flash?
breaks: Wrong if both of them still have summoners and their jungler hasn't shown: play it from the middle of the lane.
basis: pro:Deny the levels, not just the minions

when: you are at least two levels below their marksman
asks: I'm way behind bot, what do I do
can't touch the wave
I'm stuck under tower
how do I catch up as adc
say: Stay in experience range and take only safe minions until a teammate breaks the wave, or ask to swap lanes if they're diving.
more: Levels come back faster than gold. Standing near every wave, even without last hits, closes the gap enough to use your abilities again.
A top laner or jungler clearing one big wave for you resets the lane. That's the help to ask for, more than a gank.
Later, clearing waves in mid is where a weak marksman recovers, so the goal now is simply not to die again.
check: Can they dive you with the next wave, and is anyone on your team able to come?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is dead or far away and they've overextended: farm the wave at your tower normally.
basis: pro:When behind, collect levels first

when: you have at least three more kills than deaths
asks: I'm fed, can I rotate alone
should I walk to the fight
can I go through river
how do I not throw my lead
say: Move with your support through your own jungle, or stay and take the wave if nobody can walk with you.
more: A fed marksman carries a shutdown. Their jungler and mid would rather find you alone in the river than win a team fight.
One death like that hands back much of the lead and gives their weakest carry time to farm.
Arriving a few seconds later with a support is nearly always fine. Arriving dead is the only real mistake.
check: Where are their jungler and mid, and is the river warded?
breaks: Wrong if both of them just showed on the other side of the map: take the short route and get there first.
basis: pro:The fed carry does not walk alone

when: an ally died in a side lane in the last minute
asks: top just got ganked, where do I go
they killed my laner, what now
do I go help the lane that died
where do I path after that gank
say: Path to that lane and wait out of sight, because they often come back for a dive, or take the far objective if you're too far.
more: A laner back with no Flash and a bad wave is the obvious next target. Being there turns their second dive into your double kill.
Stay hidden. If they see you, they simply leave and you've spent the time; unseen, they commit with the tower hitting them.
If you can't get there, don't walk half way. Use the time their jungler spends on that side for a dragon, grubs or his camps.
check: Is the wave pushing toward your laner's tower, and did your laner lose Flash?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler shows somewhere else first: go back to your camps and tell the laner to give the wave.
basis: pro:Cover the lane they will dive again

when: their jungler has two or more kills or assists and one of your lanes has died twice
asks: where's their jungler
he's always bot, why
where will he gank next
is he coming again
say: Assume he's coming back to the lane that fed him after each clear; ward his route there, or gank the opposite side while he does.
more: Junglers repeat what works. A lane that gave kills and still has no summoners is where his next clear ends.
That makes him predictable: his camps on the other half come back untouched, and the far lane has no jungler behind it.
A ward on his entrance turns the next visit into wasted time for him, and wasted time is how a jungler's lead stops growing.
check: Which entrance did he use last time, and are his far-side camps up?
breaks: Wrong once that lane has swapped or is hugging tower: he'll look elsewhere, so track him from his camp timers instead.
basis: pro:A jungler returns to the lane that paid
